doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Tommy Newsom, the square-looking saxophonist and arranger
summary: Young recalls Tommy Newsom, whom Johnny Carson teased, as a sweet man and close friend.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: He wrote and arranged, took Doc‘s place, I mean, who‘s place did he replace? He was the leader of a band.
Yes you do. He was the leader. Sometimes when Doc wasn‘t there he would be the leader and he would be so square looking …
He would be so square looking and Johnny used to make fun of him. And Doc was a, you know.
Yeah, I know, I can see him, but I can‘t remember his name. I can see him.
Tommy was a great cat, man. He was a sweetheart of a man. But he was just so … and Doc [laughs] and Johnny used, Johnny used to pick on him, man.
Because he wouldn‘t be dressing up like Doc, or anything, he would just come in, he was very square in other words.
That‘s right, I remember now, yeah. [laughs]

But it worked. It worked, you know. I didn‘t bother Tommy. Tommy was, I loved Tommy, man. Me and Tommy got along like two brothers. We really did, man. And his wife, so sweet, I used to go out to his house and you know, hang out with them. It‘s too bad we lost Tommy, man. I haven‘t seen his wife since he passed or anything, but I think of her anyway. She‘s a very sweet woman. Tommy was… you couldn‘t beat Tommy, man. He was as nice as he looked. You remember seeing him on television. He was just so plain, man.
And just down to Earth. [laugh] He was something else.
